unit.label: Local food & recommendations
unit.title: Food Worth Trying
unit.description: 10 new words and expressions. Name local dishes, share what you know or have heard, and recommend a meal.

goal.text: 我知道那家店。你一定要吃小籠包！
goal.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nà jiā diàn. Nǐ yídìng yào chī xiǎolóngbāo!
goal.meaning: I know that shop. You really must try the xiaolongbao!

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 5, pp. 86–88; 聽說 from Lesson 6, pp. 104–106.

lessons.title: Small Steamed Dumplings
lessons.subtitle: Learn one food name and one detailed new character.

steps.prompt: Which food name contains the new character 籠?
steps.explanation: The middle syllable of 小籠包 is 籠 lóng.

steps.prompt: You want to count six individual xiaolongbao. Choose the measure word.
steps.explanation: 六個小籠包 counts six individual dumplings. 杯 counts cups; 支 was taught for phones.

steps.prompt: In 小籠包, how is 籠 pronounced?
steps.explanation: For this food name, 籠 has rising second tone: lóng.

lessons.title: A Strong-Smelling Snack
lessons.subtitle: Read all three characters in 臭豆腐.

steps.prompt: Does the word 臭豆腐 by itself tell you that the dish is spicy?
options: No; 辣 is the word for spicy.
steps.answer: No; 辣 is the word for spicy.
steps.explanation: 臭 refers to the smell here. You still need 辣 to describe spiciness.

steps.prompt: In 臭豆腐, which reading fits 臭?
steps.explanation: Use chòu, falling fourth tone, in this food name.

steps.prompt: Which says that the shop has quite a few snacks?
steps.explanation: 有不少 means there are quite a few; 沒有 means there are none.

steps.prompt: Read: 那家店的人很少。 What is small in number?
steps.explanation: The sentence names 人 before 很少, so it describes a small number of people.

steps.prompt: Choose the pronunciation of 少 in 不少.
steps.explanation: The quantity word 少 is shǎo, third tone. 不少 is bù shǎo.

lessons.title: I Know a Place
lessons.subtitle: Separate knowing information from hearing a report.

steps.prompt: You have heard a report about a restaurant. Which beginning communicates that source?
steps.explanation: 聽說 introduces information heard from others.

steps.prompt: Which says “I know how to cook,” rather than “I know that shop”?
steps.explanation: A learned skill uses 會. 知道 expresses knowing information or knowing of a place.

steps.prompt: You do not know which shop sells dumplings. Which short answer fits?
steps.explanation: The question concerns information, so answer with 不知道.

lessons.title: So Good!
lessons.subtitle: React to a description and agree with a friend.

steps.prompt: A friend says: 這家店很有名。 Choose an agreeing reply.
steps.explanation: 是啊 agrees with the statement about the shop.

steps.prompt: Choose the natural way to say “so delicious.”
steps.explanation: 這麼 directly precedes 好吃; do not add 很 or 是 here.

steps.prompt: Your friend can join the meal you planned. Which expresses happy news?
steps.explanation: 太好了 expresses delight about a welcome situation.

lessons.title: You Really Must Try It
lessons.subtitle: Make a strong recommendation and put the conversation together.

steps.prompt: Which sentence is the strong food recommendation?
steps.explanation: 一定要 makes the recommendation strong. 嗎 asks a question.

steps.prompt: Where does 一定 go in 你 __ 要吃小籠包?
steps.explanation: The taught order is person + 一定 + 要 + action.
定 is dìng, a falling fourth tone. 一定 is yídìng.

steps.prompt: Review: which means “I can cook, but I do not cook well”?
options: 我會做飯，可是做得不好。
我不會做飯，可是做得很好。
steps.answer: 我會做飯，可是做得不好。
steps.explanation: 會 states the learned skill; 得 introduces how well you do it.

lessons.title: Unit 17 Review
lessons.subtitle: Read, listen, write, and choose the right response.

steps.prompt: A friend says: 我聽說那家店的小籠包很好吃。 What does 我聽說 tell you?
options: The friend says they can cook it.
The friend says it is spicy.
steps.explanation: 聽說 introduces a report, without claiming direct experience.

steps.prompt: Which means “quite a few people”?
steps.explanation: 不少 means not few: quite a few. 很少 means few; 沒有 means none.

steps.prompt: Your friend proposes a meal you are excited about. Choose the enthusiastic reply.
steps.explanation: 太好了 welcomes the plan.

steps.prompt: Read: 我知道那家店，可是我不會做小籠包。 Which interpretation is correct?
options: I know the shop, but cannot make xiaolongbao.
I can make xiaolongbao, but do not know the shop.
I heard that the shop is expensive.
steps.answer: I know the shop, but cannot make xiaolongbao.
steps.explanation: 知道 is knowing information; 會 is learned ability.
豆 is dòu, a falling fourth tone, as in 臭豆腐.

newVocabulary.meaning: stinky tofu; fermented tofu with a strong smell
quite a few; quite a lot
to know a fact; to know of something
to hear that; to have heard that
so; this much, before a description
definitely; really must, in 一定要

籠.meaning: steamer basket; lóng in 小籠包
籠.note: In 小籠包, 籠 refers to the small steaming basket. Read this syllable lóng, with a rising tone.
籠.memory: Think of bamboo above a detailed lower block: a bamboo steamer for the buns. This is a memory aid.

parts.label: 𥫗
parts.name: bamboo top
parts.description: The six-stroke bamboo top is written as two small three-stroke groups.

parts.label: 龍
parts.name: dragon-shaped lower block
parts.description: The sixteen-stroke 龍 block fills the lower area. Keep its left upright block separate from the long shape on the right.

臭.note: Read 臭 as chòu in 臭豆腐. The name refers to the strong smell of fermented tofu.
臭.memory: The familiar 自 sits above 犬. Remember the small dot of 犬: the bottom is not just 大.

parts.label: 自
parts.name: self-shaped top
parts.description: The upper 自 has a short slant, an outer frame and two inner horizontal lines.

parts.label: 犬
parts.name: dog-shaped bottom
parts.description: The lower 犬 has four strokes, including the small dot beside the spreading strokes.

豆.note: 豆 is the bean character in the tofu name 臭豆腐. Its seven strokes make a compact, balanced shape.
豆.memory: Picture a covered vessel standing on two short supports and a wide base.

parts.label: 一
parts.name: top line
parts.description: Start with one horizontal line, separate from the box below.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: central box
parts.description: The middle box takes three strokes; close its bottom before adding the base.

parts.label: 䒑
parts.name: lower support
parts.description: Two short strokes open above a final broad horizontal baseline.

腐.note: 腐 is the last character of 臭豆腐. Learn the complete food name; translating each character literally does not give its usual food meaning.
腐.memory: A shelter surrounds a compact person-and-hand block, with the meat-shaped block at the bottom.

parts.label: 广
parts.name: shelter
parts.description: A dot and roof line lead into a long left-falling stroke around the upper part.

parts.label: 付
parts.name: upper inner block
parts.description: Inside the shelter, the two-stroke person shape stands beside the three-stroke 寸 shape.

parts.label: 肉
parts.name: meat-shaped lower block
parts.description: Write the outer frame then the two small person-like forms inside, six strokes altogether.

知.meaning: know; first syllable of 知道
知.note: 知 begins 知道, to know a fact or know of something. It is not the learned-skill word 會.
知.memory: The five-stroke arrow shape stands next to a small mouth-shaped box.

parts.label: 矢
parts.name: arrow-shaped left
parts.description: The five strokes on the left include two horizontals and two spreading lower strokes.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth-shaped right
parts.description: The right-hand box is three strokes, with its bottom closed last.

道.meaning: dào in 知道; way or path
道.note: 道 is the second character of 知道. It has 13 strokes in this Taiwan handwriting form.
道.memory: Write the upright head-shaped block first, then let the walking component carry it from the left and below.

parts.label: 首
parts.name: head-shaped inner block
parts.description: The inner 首 has two short top strokes above a horizontal and a framed lower section.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: walking component
parts.description: The Taiwan form here uses four strokes on the left and along the bottom. Follow the guide instead of merging the small strokes.

定.note: 定 forms the second syllable of 一定, definitely. In 一定要, the whole expression makes a firm recommendation.
定.memory: A three-stroke roof sits over a steady lower support.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: Write the dot, left roof stroke and hooked roof stroke first.

parts.label: 𤴓
parts.name: lower support
parts.description: Five strokes form the lower block: its central upright connects to two spreading lower strokes.

u17-dumplings.title: Name a local dish
u17-dumplings.explanation: 小籠包 (xiǎolóngbāo) are small steamed dumplings. Learn all three syllables as one food name. You already know 小 and 包 from earlier units; 籠 is the new character. For individual dumplings, use 個, as with 包子.
u17-dumplings.remember: 小籠包 is a food name. 個 counts individual pieces.

u17-tofu.title: Recognize the whole food name
u17-tofu.pattern: 吃 / 喜歡 + 臭豆腐
u17-tofu.explanation: 臭豆腐 (chòu dòufǔ) is stinky tofu, a fermented tofu snack with a strong smell. Its name does not mean it is necessarily spicy. Say 辣 when you mean spicy. Use the whole food name after 吃 or 喜歡.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng chòu dòufǔ bú là.
examples.meaning: This kind of stinky tofu is not spicy.

u17-tofu.remember: A strong smell and a spicy taste are different descriptions.

u17-quantity.title: Describe a small number
u17-quantity.pattern: noun + 很少; 很少 + noun
u17-quantity.explanation: 少 (shǎo) means few or little in quantity, opposite to 多. In 這家店的人很少, the number of people is small. 很少人 means few people. This lesson uses 少 for quantity, not for the separate idea of doing an activity rarely.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de rén hěn shǎo.
examples.meaning: There are few people at this shop.

examples.pinyin: Hěn shǎo rén xiǎng hē rè chá.

u17-quantity.remember: 少 is shǎo in quantity descriptions.

u17-quite-a-few.title: Not few means quite a few
u17-quite-a-few.pattern: 不少 + noun; 有 + 不少 + noun
u17-quite-a-few.explanation: 不少 (bù shǎo) literally means not few and is used for quite a few or quite a lot. It does not mean none. Compare 有不少小吃, there are quite a few snacks, with 沒有小吃, there are no snacks.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn yǒu bù shǎo xiǎochī.
examples.meaning: This shop has quite a few snacks.

examples.pinyin: Bù shǎo rén xǐhuān chī xiǎolóngbāo.
examples.meaning: Quite a few people like eating xiaolongbao.

u17-quite-a-few.remember: 不少 is a substantial quantity. 沒有 says there are none.

u17-know.title: Know a fact or know of a place
u17-know.explanation: 知道 (zhīdào) means know a fact or know of something. 知道那家店 means you know of that shop. It does not claim you know how to cook. For a learned skill, keep using 會 + activity. Say 不知道 for do not know; ask 知不知道 for know or not know.

examples.text: 你知不知道哪家店賣小籠包？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhī bù zhīdào nǎ jiā diàn mài xiǎolóngbāo?
examples.meaning: Do you know which shop sells xiaolongbao?

u17-know.remember: 知道 = know information. 會做飯 = know how to cook.

u17-heard.title: Share a report without claiming personal experience
u17-heard.explanation: 聽說 (tīngshuō) means hear that or have heard that. Follow it with a statement. The whole expression introduces information you heard from someone else; it does not mean listening and speaking as two separate activities.

examples.text: 我聽說那家店的小籠包很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngshuō nà jiā diàn de xiǎolóngbāo hěn hǎochī.
examples.meaning: I have heard that the xiaolongbao at that shop are delicious.

u17-heard.remember: 聽說 tells the listener that your information is something you heard.

u17-so.title: Refer to this degree of a quality
u17-so.pattern: 這麼 + description; 這麼 + 多 / 少 + noun
u17-so.explanation: 這麼 (zhème) means so or to this degree before a description. 這麼好吃 means so delicious; 這麼多人 means so many people. Unlike 真, which emphasizes really, 這麼 points to the degree being seen or discussed. Do not insert 很 between 這麼 and the description.

examples.pinyin: Zhème hǎochī, wǒ yě xiǎng chī.
examples.meaning: It is so delicious; I want to eat it too.

examples.text: 為什麼這麼多人喜歡這家店？
examples.pinyin: Wèishénme zhème duō rén xǐhuān zhè jiā diàn?
examples.meaning: Why do so many people like this shop?

u17-so.remember: Use 這麼好吃, not 這麼很好吃. 這麼 is not the question word 怎麼.

u17-agree.title: Agree with a statement
u17-agree.explanation: 是啊 (shì a) is a conversational way to agree: yes, that is right. It fits a statement such as 這家店很有名. It is not a universal replacement for every yes-answer: answer 你會做飯嗎 with 會 when you mean you can.

examples.text: 這家店很有名。— 是啊。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn hěn yǒumíng. — Shì a.
examples.meaning: This shop is well-known. — Yes, it is.

u17-agree.remember: Use 是啊 to agree with what someone has said.

u17-great.title: Welcome good news
u17-great.pattern: good news / welcome plan → 太好了！
u17-great.explanation: 太好了 (tài hǎo le) means great or wonderful. You met 太…了 with negative reactions such as 太貴了. Here 好 makes it a positive reaction to welcome news. This 了 is not a past-tense ending.

examples.text: 明天我們一起去吃小籠包。— 太好了！
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒmen yìqǐ qù chī xiǎolóngbāo. — Tài hǎo le!
examples.meaning: Tomorrow we will go eat xiaolongbao together. — Wonderful!

u17-great.remember: 太好了 is enthusiastic good news; 太貴了 complains about price.

u17-recommend.title: Make a firm recommendation
u17-recommend.explanation: 一定 (yídìng) means definitely. In 一定要 + action it strengthens a recommendation: you really must do this. In this food conversation it is enthusiastic advice, not a restaurant rule. Put 一定 before 要. 一 is pronounced yí before the fourth tone of 定.

examples.text: 你一定要吃這家的小籠包。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yídìng yào chī zhè jiā de xiǎolóngbāo.
examples.meaning: You really must try the xiaolongbao at this shop.

examples.text: 明天我一定要去那家店。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒ yídìng yào qù nà jiā diàn.
examples.meaning: I definitely want to go to that shop tomorrow.

u17-recommend.remember: 一定要 strengthens the recommendation; 想 expresses wanting.

u17-dumpling-choice.text: 你想吃小籠包還是包子？
u17-dumpling-choice.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī xiǎolóngbāo háishì bāozi?
u17-dumpling-choice.meaning: Would you like xiaolongbao or baozi?

u17-tofu-opinion.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng chòu dòufǔ hěn hǎochī.
u17-tofu-opinion.meaning: This kind of stinky tofu is delicious.

u17-tofu-spice.text: 我怕辣，所以不想吃辣的臭豆腐。
u17-tofu-spice.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, suǒyǐ bù xiǎng chī là de chòu dòufǔ.
u17-tofu-spice.meaning: I am sensitive to spicy food, so I do not want spicy stinky tofu.

u17-few-people.pinyin: Nà jiā diàn de rén hěn shǎo.
u17-few-people.meaning: There are few people at that shop.

u17-many-snacks.text: 這家店有不少好吃的小吃。
u17-many-snacks.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn yǒu bù shǎo hǎochī de xiǎochī.
u17-many-snacks.meaning: This shop has quite a few delicious snacks.

u17-know-place.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào yì jiā yǒumíng de diàn.
u17-know-place.note: 有名的店 is the familiar description + 的 + noun pattern.

u17-heard-food.text: 我聽說那家餐廳的菜不辣。
u17-heard-food.pinyin: Wǒ tīngshuō nà jiā cāntīng de cài bú là.
u17-heard-food.meaning: I have heard that the food at that restaurant is not spicy.

u17-so-expensive.text: 這家店的菜為什麼這麼貴？
u17-so-expensive.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de cài wèishénme zhème guì?
u17-so-expensive.meaning: Why is the food at this shop so expensive?

u17-great-plan.text: 太好了！我們明天一起去吧。
u17-great-plan.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù ba.
u17-great-plan.meaning: Wonderful! Let us go together tomorrow.

u17-recommend-dish.text: 你一定要吃這家的小籠包。
u17-recommend-dish.pinyin: Nǐ yídìng yào chī zhè jiā de xiǎolóngbāo.
u17-recommend-dish.meaning: You really must try the xiaolongbao at this shop.

u17-recommend-plan.text: 我知道那家店，我們明天一起去吧。
u17-recommend-plan.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nà jiā diàn, wǒmen míngtiān yìqǐ qù ba.
u17-recommend-plan.meaning: I know that shop; let us go together tomorrow.
